output.summary: KEP-383 graduates the new Event API (events.k8s.io/v1) to GA. The API was promoted from v1beta1 to v1 in 1.19, with only kube-scheduler migrated to use it at the time of the excerpt.
output.rationale: Existing Events are spammy, have unclear semantics, and can overload the API server. The new API makes semantic fields first-class for better deduplication and querying, adds series detection that sends only start and finish events, and uses a more aggressive backoff. Reviewers settled that the API itself has no feature gate, and that the client-library fallback to the old API is kept while the library is used across many clients.

alternatives.option: Gate the client-library use behind a feature gate
alternatives.why_not: Reviewer wojtek-t said a feature gate for the library was intended but never added, and that the fallback pattern should continue since the gate would be locked to true at GA.

alternatives.option: Drop the fallback to the old core Event API once GA
alternatives.why_not: liggitt said the event recorder is used by many out-of-tree clients with different skew support, so fallback makes sense, and yastij said to keep fallback for safety after GA.
wojtek-t wrote that Events have always been best-effort and the new API keeps that, so no SLO will be introduced.

evidence.quote: The new Event API has been promoted from v1beta1 to v1 in 1.19 and currently only scheduler was migrated to use it.
We've never used feature-gates for the API itself. Though, you can enable/disabled specific APIs at kube-apiserver level using --runtime-config flag.
once we move move to GA I think we should still fallback for safety. might be worth considering for other APIs
Events have always been "best-effort". We're sticking to that with the new API too. So no SLO will be introduced.
In addition, we will improve 'Event series' detection and send only 'series start' and 'series finish' Events, and add more aggressive backoff policy for Events.
